title: Thin Air, The Engadin Ridge Week

bestPeriod.note: Piz Languard's summit ridge holds snow into early July, and the high huts shut in early October.

summary: Seven days of altitude running above Pontresina, from a 1,800 m valley floor to the 3,262 m summit of Piz Languard, with lifts and rail as the safety net.
hook: The Oberengadin's valley floor sits at 1,800 metres, which means you sleep higher than most Alpine summits and everything you run starts with an advantage. It is a training environment before it is a holiday: long, graded, panoramic paths, three cable cars that sell you vertical metres, and a railway that will always take you home.

snapshot.Base(s): Pontresina, with runs from Muottas Muragl, Surlej, Sils, Morteratsch and St. Moritz
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 105-115 km and 5,200-5,800 m of ascent; larch forest track, alp meadow, granite blockfield and scree, T1-T3
snapshot.Getting There: Fly Zürich (ZRH), train via Chur and the Albula line to Pontresina (approx. 4 h)
snapshot.Who It Suits: Runners who want altitude adaptation and long climbs, not exposure and cables

itinerary.title: Val Roseg, Flat and High
itinerary.morning: Arrive in Pontresina and do nothing energetic. At 1,805 m, the first day is about drinking water and letting the resting heart rate settle.
itinerary.afternoon: Easy out-and-back up the Val Roseg on the gravel carriage road from the edge of the village to Hotel Roseg Gletscher, about 7 km each way, almost level, with the Roseg glacier tongue and Piz Bernina closing the head of the valley. T1, fully runnable, and a perfect first-day aerobic dose at 1,800-2,000 m.
itinerary.evening: Pontresina. Eat early and sleep long; altitude disrupts the first two nights.
itinerary.dayStats: 15 km, 300 m ascent, T1. Water: Hotel Roseg Gletscher (open through the summer season) and the village fountains in Pontresina, which are drinking water unless signed otherwise. **Bail-out:** horse-drawn carriages run the valley road all summer and will take a passenger.

itinerary.title: Muottas Muragl to Alp Languard
itinerary.morning: Funicular from Punt Muragl to Muottas Muragl at 2,456 m, the view down the chain of Engadin lakes to Maloja is the region's signature. Start running from the top station on the Panoramaweg that traverses east under Piz Muragl.
itinerary.afternoon: The path climbs gently to the Segantinihütte (Chamanna Segantini, 2,731 m), where the painter Giovanni Segantini died in 1899, then contours down to Alp Languard at 2,326 m. Broad, stony, T2 and largely runnable. Take the Alp Languard chairlift down or run the forest path to Pontresina.
itinerary.evening: Legs will feel heavier than the numbers justify. That is altitude, not fitness.
itinerary.dayStats: 13 km, 480 m ascent, T2. Water: Chamanna Segantini (staffed roughly late June to mid-October, drinks bought), Restaurant Alp Languard at the chairlift top station. **Bail-out:** funicular or chairlift at either end; there is no committing ground.

itinerary.title: Fuorcla Surlej and the Long Descent
itinerary.morning: Bus to Surlej, cable car to Corvatsch's Murtèl middle station at 2,702 m, then the short traverse to Fuorcla Surlej (2,755 m). The Berghaus there looks straight across at the Bernina group's north faces, Piz Roseg, Piz Scerscen, Piz Bernina in one frame.
itinerary.afternoon: Run north over the shoulder and down past the Hahnensee to St. Moritz Bad, then along the lake path to St. Moritz station. It is 1,400 m of descent on stone, alp track and finally forest, eccentric loading, and the point of the day.
itinerary.evening: Train back to Pontresina, ten minutes. Ice the quads.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 420 m ascent, 1,430 m descent, T2. Water: Berghaus Fuorcla Surlej (staffed in summer), Restaurant Hahnensee at 2,153 m. **Bail-out:** ride the Corvatsch cable car back down instead of descending.

itinerary.title: Sils, the Lakes and Val Fex
itinerary.morning: Postbus down the valley to Sils Maria. Run the shoreline path along the Silsersee and out onto the Chastè peninsula, where the Nietzsche stone sits among the larches, flat, soft, T1.
itinerary.afternoon: Turn up the Val Fex on the near-level valley road to Fex Crasta and its 15th-century church, then back. A genuine recovery day at 1,800-2,000 m, which is the whole reason to sit in the Engadin rather than train at sea level.
itinerary.evening: Sils Maria for cake, then the bus home. Nothing after 20:00.
itinerary.dayStats: 17 km, 260 m ascent, T1, entirely runnable. Water: village fountains in Sils Maria and Fex Crasta. **Bail-out:** postbus stops at Sils, Silvaplana and along the Val Fex road.

itinerary.title: Peak Day: Piz Languard, 3,262 m
itinerary.morning: Leave Pontresina at first light on the direct path towards Alp Languard, then up the long, graded zigzags past Chamanna Paradis at 2,540 m. This is 1,460 m of continuous climbing, T2 on the lower half and T3 on the granite blockfield above the hut, with a marked but hands-on final ridge to the summit.
itinerary.afternoon: From the top the whole Bernina massif, the Morteratsch and Pers glaciers and, on a clear day, a line of peaks into Italy. Descend to Alp Languard, then take the Panoramaweg west past the Segantinihütte to Muottas Muragl and down the Schafberg path to Punt Muragl.
itinerary.evening: Pontresina. Eat everything. This is the hardest single day of the week by a wide margin.
itinerary.dayStats: 22 km, 1,600 m ascent, T3 above 2,800 m. Water: Chamanna Paradis (small and not always staffed, treat as unreliable), Chamanna Segantini on the return. Carry 2 l. **Bail-out:** turn at Chamanna Paradis; descend to Alp Languard and ride the chairlift, or take the funicular down from Muottas Muragl.

itinerary.title: Chamanna Boval and the Glacier Front
itinerary.morning: Train two stops to Morteratsch. Run the Gletscherweg up the moraine, past the year-markers showing where the glacier stood in 1900, 1950 and 2000, then climb the lateral moraine path to Chamanna Boval at 2,495 m, an SAC hut hung directly above the ice.
itinerary.afternoon: Return by the same route or the higher variant, then run the flat valley path back to Pontresina through the larch woods rather than taking the train. Roughly 800 m of climbing on tired legs.
itinerary.dayStats: 16 km, 820 m ascent, T3 on the moraine, T2 below. Water: Chamanna Boval (staffed roughly late June to mid-October; water is bought). **Bail-out:** the Morteratsch station and the Diavolezza cable car are both within reach of the valley floor.

itinerary.title: Stazerwald and Home
itinerary.morning: Easy loop from Pontresina through the Stazerwald larch forest to the Lej da Staz and on to St. Moritz, soft, level, T1, 40 minutes of genuine shakeout at 1,800 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Train from St. Moritz over the Albula line to Chur and Zürich. Sit on the right leaving St. Moritz for the Landwasser viaduct.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 180 m ascent, T1. Water: fountains in Pontresina and St. Moritz Dorf.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Saratz
accommodationStrategy.description: A 19th-century house with a modern wing, a large park, indoor and outdoor pools and a sauna, the recovery infrastructure that a 5,500 m week actually needs. It sits directly on the Val Roseg and Alp Languard trailheads, so three days start on foot from the door.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: CHF 250-420 (approx. €260, €440) per night for two, half board available

accommodationStrategy.name: Romantik Hotel Muottas Muragl
accommodationStrategy.description: Reached only by funicular and sitting 650 m above the valley floor, which turns two or three nights here into real altitude exposure rather than daytime visits. Sunrise runs on the Panoramaweg start outside the front door.
accommodationStrategy.booking: three months ahead; there are very few rooms.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: CHF 300-450 (approx. €310, €470) per night for two, half board

accommodationStrategy.name: Jugendherberge Pontresina
accommodationStrategy.description: A large, well-run hostel with private rooms, half board included, a drying room and gear storage, five minutes from the station. The cheapest way to spend a week in one of the most expensive valleys in the Alps.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: CHF 90-130 (approx. €95, €135) per person per night with half board

logistics.emergency: works; the number that matters in the Swiss mountains is **1414** for Rega helicopter rescue. A Rega patronage costs about CHF 40 a year and removes the argument about who pays.

Most Engadin hotels include the summer mountain railways and regional buses in the room rate through the regional guest card, Muottas Muragl, Corvatsch, Diavolezza and Alp Languard among them. Confirm it at booking; it is worth well over CHF 200 across a week.
The Rhaetian Railway runs Pontresina-Morteratsch-St. Moritz frequently, and PostAuto covers the lakes. Both are punctual to the minute; the timetable is a contract, not a suggestion.
Weather flips fast at 3,000 m. MeteoSwiss and the SAC's hut pages are the two sources to check the night before and the morning of; afternoon convective storms build from late July.
SAC huts including Chamanna Boval take reservations online and by phone. Even for a day visit, water and food are bought, not free, and cash is still welcome.
Village fountains in Graubünden are drinking water by default; anything not potable is signed *kein Trinkwasser*. Glacier meltwater is heavy with rock flour, do not drink it.

Nothing in this itinerary enters the Swiss National Park, but if you add it, be aware its rules are the strictest in the Alps: no leaving the path, no running off-trail, no dogs, no bivouac. Wild camping is also restricted across much of Graubünden above the treeline.
Mobile coverage is good on the lift-served ridges and unreliable in the Val Roseg and the upper Morteratsch valley.

proTips: Spend the first 48 hours below 2,500 m. The Val Roseg and Sils days exist to let haemoglobin adapt before Piz Languard, and skipping them is why people bonk at 3,000 m on day three.
Take the first Muottas Muragl funicular and run the Panoramaweg eastwards in the morning. It faces south-west, so the afternoon light is better but the heat and the crowds are worse.
Ride the lifts up and run down on Day 3, then reverse the pattern on Day 5. Alternating loading direction across the week is what keeps quads intact through a seven-day block.
Buy the Corvatsch and Diavolezza rides as part of the guest card rather than at the counter, walk-up single fares in the Engadin run CHF 30-50 each.
The Val Roseg carriage road is the region's best tempo surface: 14 km of near-flat, well-drained gravel at 1,900 m, with no traffic and no navigation.
If Piz Languard is snowbound or stormy, substitute Piz Nair from Corviglia, lift-assisted, 3,057 m, and a fraction of the commitment.
Book the Segantinihütte or Chamanna Boval for lunch by phone in high season; both are small and both fill with walkers from 12:00.

packingNotes: Shoes with a real rock plate for the Piz Languard blockfield and the Boval moraine, Engadin granite is angular and unforgiving.
Two-litre carrying capacity for Day 5; 750 ml is plenty on the lift-served days.
A warm layer and a proper wind shell. It can be 25°C in Pontresina and near freezing on the Languard ridge in the same hour.
Sun protection at strength. UV at 3,000 m is brutal, and the Engadin averages more sunshine than almost anywhere in Switzerland.
Light gloves and a beanie for the summit ridge, even in August.
Swiss francs in small notes for hut drinks; card acceptance at 2,700 m is inconsistent.
Poles for the Languard climb and the 1,400 m Fuorcla Surlej descent.
A head torch for the pre-dawn start on Day 5.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Altitude hits harder than expected.** Headache, poor sleep and a raised resting heart rate are normal for 48 hours. If they persist, drop Day 5 to the Muottas Muragl traverse and try Piz Languard on Day 6 instead.
**Afternoon thunderstorm on the Languard ridge.** The summit block is exposed granite. Be off the top by noon; the escape is straight down to Chamanna Paradis and Alp Languard.
**Early snow.** A September cold front can put 20 cm on everything above 2,800 m overnight. The lake paths at Sils and the Val Roseg stay runnable in any conditions.
**Lift closures.** Corvatsch, Diavolezza and Alp Languard each have a short summer season and maintenance days. Check operating dates before planning a day around a descent you have not earned.
**Sticker shock.** Switzerland at altitude is expensive. Half-board rates and the hostel option are what make a seven-day block affordable; buying lunch at 2,700 m every day is not.
